title: 5.1.25 Lab: A grid like math (optional)
description: Optional: a preview of an optional mode. Draw a grid over the canvas, then switch it to math mode, where (0, 0) is the centre and y grows up. Nothing after this lab needs it, and it is not graded.

steps.title: Draw the grid
steps.instructions: This lab is optional: it previews a mode the rest of the course does not use. Click Run first. The starter already works: a 400 by 400 canvas, painted dark. Now, inside draw(), on the line after `background('#222');`, add `showGrid(50);` and Run again. It draws a light grid with a line every 50 pixels and numbers along the top and left edges. Read it: (0, 0) is the top-left corner, x grows to the right, and y grows DOWN, so a bigger y is lower on the canvas. That is the default, the same as the browser's own canvas and every sketch you have made so far. showGrid() goes in draw(), not setup(): it draws for one frame at a time, so draw() has to ask for it every frame.
hints: Open the moSHion docs drawer on the right and find the Coordinates section.

steps.title: Switch on math mode
steps.instructions: In setup(), on the line right after `new Canvas(400, 400);`, add `world.origin = 'math';` and Run. Look at the grid again. The two brighter, thicker lines (the axes) now cross in the CENTRE of the canvas, and that point is (0, 0). x still grows to the right, but y grows UP: the numbers above the centre are positive and the ones below it are negative, like a graph in math class. The line has to come before you make any sprite. If it comes after one, the sketch stops with an error that tells you to move it up.
hints: Spell it exactly: world, a dot, origin, then = 'math' with the quotes.
Put it on the very next line after new Canvas(400, 400); so it comes before any sprite.

steps.title: Place a sprite at (100, 50)
steps.instructions: Below the math-mode line, still inside setup(), make a sprite and store it in `box` (the starter already declares `let box;`): `box = new Sprite(100, 50, 40, 40);`. Give it a color too if you like, as in 5.1.11. Run it. The sprite sits 100 to the right of the centre and 50 ABOVE it, because a positive y means up in math mode. Check it against the grid. In the default mode the same two numbers would put it in the top-left quarter of the canvas instead.
hints: The second number is y. In math mode a positive y is above the centre, so 50 puts the sprite a little above the middle.

steps.title: Show the mouse
steps.instructions: In draw(), on the line after `showGrid(50);`, add `showMouse();` and Run. Move the mouse over the canvas: the numbers beside the pointer are its (x, y). Find (0, 0) in the centre. Then find a spot where both numbers are negative: it is below and to the left of the centre. Rest the pointer on your sprite: it reads close to (100, 50).
hints: The numbers only appear after the mouse has moved over the canvas.

steps.title: What else changes in math mode
steps.instructions: Nothing to type here. Two more things turn around in math mode, for when you meet them later. A positive rotation turns a sprite counter-clockwise, the way angles go in math class. And a world where things fall needs world.gravity.y = -10, with a minus sign, because down is negative now. The rest of the course uses the default mode, with (0, 0) at the top-left and y growing down, so you can leave math mode here.
hints: To go back to the default mode, delete the world.origin line.

requirements.title: Draw the grid
requirements.description: draw() calls showGrid(), so the grid is drawn every frame. Any spacing counts; the lab uses 50.
requirements.hint: showGrid(50); goes on its own line inside draw(). In setup() it would show for one frame and vanish.

requirements.title: Switch on math mode
requirements.description: The sketch sets world.origin to 'math'. Single quotes, double quotes or backticks all count.
requirements.hint: In setup(), on the line right after new Canvas(400, 400);, set world.origin to the word math in quotes.

requirements.title: A sprite above the centre
requirements.description: A sprite is made with a positive second number, its y, such as new Sprite(100, 50, 40, 40). In math mode a positive y is above the centre. Help: 5.1.6 (Sprite: new Sprite(x, y, w, h) + .color)
requirements.hint: The second number inside new Sprite( ) is y. Make it a number above 0, like 50.

requirements.title: Show the mouse
requirements.description: draw() calls showMouse(), which writes the pointer's (x, y) beside it.
requirements.hint: showMouse(); goes inside draw(). Move the mouse over the canvas to see the numbers.

aiCheck.rubricTitle: What the AI read in your code
aiCheck.prompt: The student wrote a moSHion sketch (p5-style JavaScript with a physics world) for the lab "5.1.25 Lab: A grid like math (optional)". The task they were given: An optional lab. In draw(), after the background, call showGrid(50) to draw a grid. In setup(), on the line right after new Canvas(400, 400), switch on math mode with world.origin set to 'math', so (0, 0) is the centre and y grows up. Below that, still in setup(), make a sprite at (100, 50), 40 by 40, and store it in box. In draw(), call showMouse() so the pointer's (x, y) shows beside it. What the starter file already had: `let box;` at the top, a 400 by 400 canvas in setup(), and background('#222') in draw(), with step comments and nothing else. The starter meets none of the criteria. You cannot run their code: read it and judge what it WOULD do when the sketch runs. Judge each criterion by whether the idea is achieved, however the student wrote it. Different variable and function names, if / else chains or ternaries, helper functions, template strings, arrow functions, semicolons, spacing, quotes and order are all fine. Do not require any particular structure unless the criterion names one. Mark a criterion missing only when the idea is absent or the code does the opposite. Code inside a comment or inside a string never runs, so a line the student only wrote in a comment does not count. moSHion facts that matter here: showGrid(spacing) and showMouse() draw for one frame at a time, so they belong in draw(), which runs every frame; called only in setup() they show for one frame and vanish. world.origin can only be 'screen' (the default: (0, 0) at the top-left, y grows down) or 'math' ((0, 0) at the centre, y grows up). Setting it after a sprite has been made, after gravity has been turned on, or once frames have run stops the sketch with an error that says to move the line up. In math mode a positive y is above the centre. Write each note for THIS student's own code: in a not-met note, name the exact line or name in their code that causes the problem (quote at most a few words of it), say in plain words what it does now versus what the criterion needs, and give one concrete next thing to try, but do NOT write the corrected code. In a met note, say in one short phrase what in their code satisfied it. Do not use generic praise. Write for a 14-year-old reader: short sentences and plain, everyday words.

rubric.title: Draw the grid
rubric.description: showGrid(...) is called inside draw(), with any spacing (the lab uses 50). A call only in setup() shows for one frame and vanishes, so it is not met.

rubric.title: Switch on math mode
rubric.description: world.origin is set to the word math in quotes (single, double or backticks), before any sprite is made, normally right after new Canvas(...) in setup(). If it comes after a sprite is made, the sketch would stop with an error, so that is not met yet.

rubric.title: A sprite above the centre
rubric.description: A sprite is made with new Sprite(...) whose second number, its y, is above 0, such as the lab's (100, 50). In math mode a positive y is above the centre. Any positive y and any x count, and storing it in box is what the step asks but is not needed for this card. Help: 5.1.6 (Sprite: new Sprite(x, y, w, h) + .color)

rubric.title: Show the mouse
rubric.description: showMouse() is called inside draw(), so the pointer's (x, y) is written beside it every frame.
